leads.summary: Open PR #6525 edits the same parser hunk and retains the string-blind trailing-comma regex
leads.consequence: The two first-function rewrites conflict when stacked. PR #6525 scans comments correctly but finishes with out.replace(/,(\s*[}\]])/g, '$1'); if that expression wins conflict resolution after #13255, a value such as 'x, ]y' is corrupted again. A combined patch needs #6525's comment handling followed by #13255's string-aware comma handling, not the older regex. #6525's added parse-error warning is a separate non-conflicting change.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q5, composition runs); corroborated, published under Related PRs; factual

leads.summary: Open PR #13305 independently implements the same string-aware trailing-comma fix in the identical hunk
leads.consequence: Both PRs replace the same initial regex with distinct string scanners against the same base. Stacking unmodified hunks requires conflict resolution; taking either complete scanner preserves commas in quoted values. #13305 does not add a JSONC parser regression test (its test change covers an unrelated editor flag). This is duplicate work and merge coordination, not a proven additional runtime defect.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q5, byte-identical equivalence runs); coordinator confirmed #13305 open at bcd1ee3 via gh; published under Related PRs; factual

leads.summary: Existing menu tests do not pin the valid quoted-comma regression
leads.consequence: The suite only asserts comments and structural trailing commas in the synthetic parser input, not a comma inside a JSON string followed by whitespace and a closing bracket or brace. It would pass with the old corrupting regex, so a future regression of this specific fix is not detected. Add a parsed-value assertion with a label/action containing ', ]' and an escaped-quote case near the existing parser test.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** The new `stripJsonc` scanner fixes #13250. A comma inside a string that is followed by `]` or `}` (with or without whitespace between) is now kept, and real trailing commas outside strings are still removed. For every valid file the old function handled correctly, the new output is byte-identical.

```text
input string          "x, ]y"          "mv ~/x.conf{.bak,}"
base  stripJsonc      "x ]y"           "mv ~/x.conf{.bak}"     comma inside the string removed
head  stripJsonc      "x, ]y"          "mv ~/x.conf{.bak,}"    string kept
```

The second column is a realistic case beyond the issue's label: a bash brace expansion with an empty last alternative in an `action` was silently changed into a different command. None of the strings in the shipped `default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc` match the pattern, so today only user menu extensions are affected.

**Verified:** Checked in isolated Node runs and in Qt's QML engine (`qml -a core`, importing `MenuModel.js` directly), the engine the shell uses to load it through `Menu.qml`:
- 400,000 generated valid JSONC documents (random whitespace including CRLF, full-line comments containing quotes and brackets, trailing commas at every nesting level, strings with escapes, brackets, commas and non-ASCII characters). The new function gave the expected text for all of them. Wherever the old function was also correct, the two outputs are byte-identical. The old function was wrong exactly on the documents with a comma followed by a closer inside a string.
- 400,000 randomly mutated, mostly invalid documents: old and new accept and reject exactly the same inputs.
- The shipped menu strips to byte-identical text on base and head and parses to the same 340 items.
- In the QML engine, a 6,036-input corpus (the hand-written cases plus generated and mutated documents from the same generators) gives the same output as in Node for both the old and new function.
- `menu-test.sh` and `menu-guards-test.sh` pass on base, on head, and on the current `quattro` tip with this PR merged.

**Optional test improvement:** `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` covers comment lines and structural trailing commas but has no comma inside a string, so it passes on the buggy base and would not catch a return of #13250. These assertions, in the same `run_node_test` harness, fail on base (`actual:   x ]y`) and pass on head:

```js
const rows = menu.parseMenuJsonc('{\n  "b": { "label": "x, ]y", "action": "mv f{.bak,}" },\n}')
assertEqual(rows[0].label, 'x, ]y', 'menu keeps a comma before ] inside a label')
assertEqual(rows[0].action, 'mv f{.bak,}', 'menu keeps a comma before } inside an action')
```

**Related PRs:**
- #13305 is a second fix for #13250 that rewrites the same `stripJsonc` lines. Its output matched this PR's on every generated, mutated and hand-written input. Whichever lands first makes the other conflict and become redundant.
- #6525 (inline comments) also rewrites these lines, keeps the old comma regex, and so still has the #13250 bug on its own. The two compose as the description says, provided the merged function strips comments before the comma scan. In the reverse order the comma scan also sees inline comments, so some valid files are rejected: for example, a trailing comma just before a `// comment`, or a lone `"` inside a comment followed by a later trailing comma.

**Optional:** The per-character scan is slower than the regex it replaces. In the QML engine, parsing the shipped 54 KB menu took about 1 to 2 ms on base and about 7 to 19 ms on head. It runs only at shell start, when a menu file changes and on `omarchy menu refresh`, not when the menu opens, so this is not user-visible. If speed matters, a single string-aware regex in place of the comma `.replace` gave byte-identical output to the scanner on the 200,000 generated valid documents it was compared on, and parsed the shipped menu in about 3 ms (warmed median):

```js
.replace(/("(?:[^"\\]|\\[\s\S])*")|,(?=\s*[}\]])/g, "$1")
```

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned head `9c0e638` against merge base `d201fb9`, plus the current `quattro` tip `c5b4db7` with this PR merged.
- Isolated Node runs of `stripJsonc` and `parseMenuJsonc`: 36 hand-written edge cases, generated and mutated documents, the shipped menu and the sample extension. For generated documents, correctness was checked against expected text without relying on `JSON.parse`.
- Qt QML engine: `qml -a core` runs of the reproduction, the input corpus and timing, on one machine with Qt 6.11.2. No Quickshell session or menu UI was started.
- Related PRs: merge simulation of this PR against the other open PRs that touch `MenuModel.js`, and generated-input comparison with #13305 and with a combination of #6525 and this PR.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
